{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-oh-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"4ad489759b13e443c27ae86c126dac5ecf80ab2b07a1ae1d123ce0431b328d73","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-oh-class-d:lineage:6","source_registry_sha256":"33124b165dc74fabcff4bbcd8fd15db36bbe4a69a10e7def76a9d71752a5128b","source_liveness_sha256":null},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Be alert","heading":"Be alert — C2","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A17
A second adult-device offense within two years carries three license points and a fine of up to two hundred fifty dollars. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A17
A third or later adult-device offense within two years carries four license points, a fine of up to five hundred dollars and a possible ninety-day license suspension. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A17
Fines for the described adult-device violations double when the violation happens in a work zone. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A17
Drivers younger than eighteen generally cannot use electronic devices even hands-free while driving, stopped at a traffic light or waiting in a traffic jam, subject to the stated exceptions. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A17
The device-use exceptions for drivers younger than eighteen allow navigation-device use and calls to emergency services. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A17
A younger driver's prohibited device use is a primary offense that can itself be the reason for a traffic stop. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A17
A first violation of the younger-driver device law carries a sixty-day license suspension and a fine of one hundred fifty dollars. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A17
A second violation of the younger-driver device law carries a one-year license suspension and a fine of three hundred dollars. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A17
Ohio prohibits operating a motor vehicle under the influence of alcohol, drugs or both. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A17
A medicine can affect driving ability even when it is legally prescribed or sold without a prescription. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A18
Alcohol and drugs may blur vision and impair focusing or judging distance, speed and other vehicles' movement. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A18
Alcohol and drugs slow the processing of information and the response to driving demands. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A18
Alcohol and drugs reduce awareness of the surroundings and the ability to make quick decisions. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0018]

Confusables: a hands-free allowance does not erase the younger-driver restriction. Phone-to-ear calls are a listed adult exception with an activation condition. Mnemonic: eyes, hands, mind. Glossary: fatigue is tiredness; aggression is intentional endangerment; distraction diverts attention. These terms and distinctions restate the cited facts without adding exceptions.
